candidates.name: Directed evolution with yeast surface display and alternating-pH selection
candidates.scope: Use a displayed Fcab library with positive selection for Her2 binding at pH 7.4 and negative selection/non-binding at pH 6.0, followed by clone-level pH-dependent binding characterization.

data.detail: Underlying clone-level screening and selection datasets have not been independently retrieved for FrontierLab.

code.detail: The evaluated route is primarily an experimental directed-evolution workflow; no required computational code artifact has been established from the current source review.

environment.detail: Laboratory platform details and instrument settings have not been independently normalized into a reproducible FrontierLab environment record.

parameters.detail: The source-derived comparison identifies alternating selection at pH 7.4 for binding and pH 6.0 for non-binding as central design parameters.

protocol.detail: The published study reports directed evolution using yeast surface display followed by characterization of isolated pH-sensitive Fcab variants.

metrics.detail: The source reports pH-dependent binding characterization and downstream assessment of isolated variants; FrontierLab has not reproduced these measurements.

comparison.expected_value: Explores sequence space without requiring a predefined histidine-centered mechanism and can reveal non-obvious pH-switching variants.
comparison.resources: Requires a physical display library, sorting workflow, recombinant target and downstream clone expression and characterization.
comparison.validation: Compare binding across acidic and physiological pH, then verify isolated variants with independent soluble-protein or cell-based assays.
comparison.limitations: Experimentally intensive and sensitive to library composition, target format, selection pressure and sorting thresholds; AI is supportive rather than central to the core search loop.
comparison.novelty: Strong comparator for mechanism diversity because the reported Fcab examples include pH-sensitive variants without histidine mutations.

candidates.name: Structure-based dual-pH histidine-scanning computational design
candidates.scope: Use an antibody-antigen structural model to perform dual-pH histidine-scanning design, prioritize variants in silico, and then validate Fab, cell-surface and full-antibody behavior across acidic and physiological pH.

data.detail: The complete design inputs, intermediate candidate-ranking outputs and raw validation datasets have not yet been independently packaged for FrontierLab.

code.detail: Availability and reproducibility of the original ADAPT implementation or an equivalent executable design stack have not yet been independently verified.

environment.detail: The exact computational environment, protonation/modeling settings and dependency versions have not yet been reconstructed.

parameters.detail: The source-derived method centers on structure-based dual-pH histidine scanning and comparison of acidic versus physiological pH binding behavior.

protocol.detail: The published workflow links computational design to Fab and full-antibody validation, including cell-based and functional assays.

metrics.detail: Reported validation includes pH-dependent binding/selectivity readouts; FrontierLab has not reproduced these measurements and must treat apparent cell-binding affinity cautiously where avidity or stoichiometry can confound interpretation.

comparison.expected_value: Provides a targeted in-silico-to-in-vitro design path in which AI can assist structure interpretation, candidate prioritization and explicit reasoning over pH-dependent design constraints before laboratory validation.
comparison.resources: Requires a structural model, a reproducible design implementation or equivalent computational stack, recombinant expression and orthogonal binding and functional validation.
comparison.validation: Validate prioritized variants across pH using Fab-level measurements, cell-based assays and full-antibody tests; add an orthogonal biophysical assay such as SPR on monomeric Fab where feasible to separate intrinsic affinity from avidity effects.
comparison.limitations: Depends on structural-model quality and a histidine-centered search assumption; apparent cell-binding affinity can be influenced by avidity/stoichiometry, so orthogonal validation is required before mechanistic interpretation.
comparison.novelty: Best fit for the FrontierLab demo because it exposes a complete AI-assisted design-to-validation chain while making uncertainty, experimental handoff and falsification visible.

Availability and reproducibility of the original ADAPT implementation or an equivalent executable design stack have not yet been independently verified.
The exact computational environment, protonation/modeling settings and dependency versions have not yet been reconstructed.

rationale: Researcher selected M2 because its structure-based computational design creates the clearest in-silico-to-in-vitro AI-for-Science demonstration: an AI agent can reason over a structural model, prioritize dual-pH histidine-scanning variants, and hand candidates to experimental Fab, cell, full-antibody and functional validation. This produces a stronger end-to-end FrontierLab narrative than M1, whose core search loop depends more heavily on physical library generation and FACS screening. M1 is retained as a comparator because it can reveal histidine-independent pH-switching solutions and therefore exposes the selected method's histidine-centered bias. M2's assay limitations are treated as a validation requirement rather than ignored: downstream planning should include an orthogonal biophysical check such as SPR on monomeric Fab where feasible to distinguish intrinsic affinity from avidity/stoichiometry effects.
